subject: Reserved capacity tranche activation + price-collar approval request (Acme.AI)
messages:
From: Jordan Rivers <jrivers@acme.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@procureops.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing for launch - initial reserve ask

Karthik, thanks for the call this morning.

We need to firm up a reserved-capacity approach for our Q4 consumer launch. High level: 8M inference requests per day, peak windows with 180ms P95 target, and an expected steady-state token mix that skews short but with intermittent longer-ctx batch jobs (NLP retraining ops).

Our procurement team would prefer a staged commit: two tranches (phase 1 + phase 2 activation) spaced over 3 months. We want pricing protection in the contract if GPU spot/retail market jumps more than 15% over baseline — something like a price-collar rather than a full indexation.

Attached are the baseline traffic projections and our internal procurement checklist. Can you share what discount bands are possible for a two-tranche activation and what approvals we'd need for a deeper concession?

Thanks,
Jordan
--
Jordan Rivers
Head of Platform, Acme.AI
jrivers@acme.ai
Attachment: acme_baseline_traffic.csv (text/csv)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@procureops.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_k@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing for launch - initial reserve ask

Jordan — really appreciate the detail. Quick read-through and a couple of clarifying items:

- Are you expecting both tranches to be equal capacity, or is phase 1 a smaller canary (we proposed 30% activation)?
- For the price-collar, what baseline are you evaluating against (our internal list price on the effective date, or a 90-day trailing market average)?

High-level response: we can structure the commitment as staged activations (canary -> ramp) and offer tiered discounts tied to committed GPU hours per tranche. For price-sensitivity we typically propose one of three constructs: (a) indexation to a published GPU index (pass-through), (b) fixed price collar with an agreed band and a partial rebate within the collar, or (c) capped retail pass-through with a short-term credit if price spikes exceed threshold.

I'll pull the numbers and loop Neha (pricing) and Kim (finance approvals) for an approvals path. Expect a draft tranche schedule + pricing sketch by EOD tomorrow.

— Karthik

From: neha_kapoor <neha_k@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 08:19:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity tranche activation + pricing sketch request

Karthik / Kim — prelim math below for ACME-3487 based on Jordan's 8M req/day peak profile and our Aurora L model config:

- Phase 1 (canary): 30% committed (24 weeks ramp window), expected util 60% -> reserved GPU hours: 42k/mo equivalent. Discount band (list price): 18% if committed for 12 months, 12% for 6 month minimum.
- Phase 2 (ramp): additional 70% activation after 90 days. If customer signs both tranches upfront for a total 12-month commitment, we can ladder to 23% discount on tranche pricing (requires finance exec sign-off).

Price-collar construct suggestion (to limit GPU market risk for Redwood):
- Baseline = Redwood published list at contract effective date.
- Collar band = +/- 12% for first 6 months; if GPU market input price moves above +12% we apply a 50% rebate on the incremental delta up to +25%; above +25% we revert to on-demand pricing for incremental usage (with a 30-day notice).

Approvals required: any aggregate discount >20% must be approved by VP Finance (Kimberly) and sign-off from Head of Sales Ops (Marissa). Any additional credit/escrow mechanisms must be legal-approved (I will flag to Legal once we finalize wording).

I attached a tranche schedule workbook (capacity_tranche_schedule.xlsx) with monthly reserved-hour estimates and sensitivity lines.

— Neha

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity tranche activation + price-collar approval request (Acme.AI)

Jordan / Lisa — attaching a clean sketch of the staged-activation commercial and the price-collar proposal (see "ACME-3487_term_sheet_v1.pdf"). Highlights:

- Phase 1: 30% activation at 18% discount (6-month minimum).
- Phase 2: additional 70% activation; if both tranches are agreed and paid upfront for 12 months, blended discount reaches 23% (subject to exec approval).
- Price-collar: +/-12% band with rebate mechanics for the +12% to +25% window. Above +25% incremental consumption will be billed at on-demand with notice.
- Burst pool: customers can consume additional on-demand burst capacity; we'll provide a 10% burst credit on committed GPU-hours if they frequently exceed committed peaks (subject to ops guardrails).

Next steps: Jordan, if this framing is acceptable, can you confirm whether ACME wants to sign both tranches now or proceed with a canary-first approach? If they want the deeper blended discount, I'll route for a >20% discount approval with Kim and Marissa.

— Karthik

Thanks — this is clear and reasonable. Two quick asks from Acme procurement: (1) move the collar to +/- 10% if possible (ProcureOps prefers tighter bands), and (2) can we add a performance SLA credit tied to P95 latency >200ms during peak windows? That will be critical for our internal product team sign-off.

We'd like to sign both tranches upfront if the blended number can get to ~24% effective discount net of burst credits and the collar is tightened. If you can route that approval this week we can get this on our July procurement board.

Jordan

Subject: RE: Reserved capacity tranche activation + price-collar approval request (ACME-3487)

Karthik — reviewed the sketch. Two comments for routing and an approval ask:

1) Discount cap approval: We can move to an effective 24% blended discount if legal accepts the tightened collar language and we implement a 6-month escrow/credit holdback that recoups excess exposure if GPU input price runs >+18% in months 1-6. That escrow mechanism reduces Redwood's risk.

2) SLA addition: I approve adding a P95 latency credit for peak windows (definition must be explicit — e.g., measured across production token-serving nodes with a 1 hour rolling window). Any SLA credit beyond a 5% invoice reduction requires CSOps sign-off.

Action for Karthik: please prepare an approval memo (one page) with the following bullets: (a) deal economics and lift to revenue, (b) proposed escrow mechanism and trigger math, (c) legal redline ask for collar wording, and (d) CSOps engagement note. Send to me and Marissa — if acceptable I'll sign for VP Finance and route to Legal for redlines.

— Kim
